## Research question

Generated SQL can execute while using the wrong database values or omitting requirements from the question.

## Method

PV-SQL issues targeted database probes, summarizes observations, extracts a checklist from question patterns, and generates SQL. Syntax, execution and construct checks guide bounded repairs. The paper describes ten constraint categories; these checks cover only part of a request’s semantics.

## Evaluation

Experiments use development sets: 1,534 BIRD questions, its 500-example Mini-Dev subset, and 1,034 Spider questions. Six LLMs, seven framework baselines, component ablations and token/latency measurements are reported. EX compares execution results with gold SQL; VES additionally measures query efficiency.

## What the results support

With GPT-4o, BIRD EX is 65.12, versus 62.13 without probing and 61.80 without repair. Gains are not universal: Qwen3-0.6B performs below zero-shot CoT. Gold-derived oracle constraints repair 15.7% of previously failed cases in a diagnostic experiment.

## Limits and qualifications

The 99.39% extraction score is gold-SQL checklist pass rate, not completeness or semantic accuracy; repair success and regression are constraint-level measures. Equivalent SQL can use different constructs, while matching constructs can still express the wrong intent. GPT-4.1-mini VES differs between tables, and released verification differs from the paper description. No held-out test, user-clarification or unanswerability evaluation is reported.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Adjacent evidence for database-grounded verification and repair, with explicit limits on checklist coverage, model dependence and reproducibility.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.

Appendix E derives oracle constraints from gold SQL and fixes 15.7% of previously failed cases; this is not a measured deployment recall rate. | Section 4.3/Table 2, PDF page 5; Table 7/Section 6.4, pages 7–8; Limitations, page 9; Tables 9–10, page 12; Appendix E, page 13 | Treat the checklist as a partial heuristic.
